# App-launched narrated screenshots

6 October 2026: the separate [current installed Wayland comparison](../../../../docs/verification/current-wayland-screenshots/README.md) replaces the synthetic selection boundary for a saved-conversation probe with actual virtual F10 and the real Omarchy picker. Eight source/native states, full selected/annotated PNG and RGBA bytes, fresh narration WAV/OCR, History/clipboard preservation and Escape/normal-Quit cleanup match the installed 2.1.0 payload with Python blocked. It adds no native owner or fixture changes; the X11 joined cases and their historical checkpoint below retain their scope. Physical audio/keys and full platform acceptance remain open.

`make linux-screenshot-test` runs four fresh native application sessions, then the existing [screenshot ownership comparison](application-screenshots-evidence.md). The new [independent fixture](released-application-images.json), SHA-256 `31767df76df28286f450984685d395ffa631469542a2982745937564f219895f`, records **seventeen states and four complete-window images** from unchanged v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Minimum 420×520 dark, narrow 480×640 light and wide 1060×780 dark images all match with zero differing pixels, without masks. Their full 8-bit RGBA hashes are saved from the independent reference captures and checked by the native target. A fourth scenario covers preparation failure before audio starts. Visual inspection retains a released minimum-size limitation: the second image's Remove control is partially clipped; matching that view does not establish a usability improvement.

The temporary reference observer verifies all 77 released modules before activation and imported paths/digests after shutdown. It drives actual application actions, widgets, editor accessibility actions and private X11 input; no application handler or service is replaced. The native observer uses the existing assembled application and shutdown owner. Both launch the actual Tensaku artifact through the unchanged production editor-wrapper template. Its SHA-256 is `79de63b635ec5a711bb250bb4fa7cd2dd69aeeb70dffe735a39c3669f7082831`; GTK 4.22.4 and Pango 1.58.2 are recorded. Separate native processes supply only external PCM, selection and Codex boundaries, with speech HTTP on private loopback. Source collectors remain under ignored `tmp/`.

The wide flow continues a saved conversation, invokes the real screenshot bridge from another process and navigates away while the picker waits. The editor opens the resulting managed image; its actual first-use dialog, Add narration, dragged text area and Stop narration run the Rust annotation helper while the original recording remains active. The saved PNG bytes match the release exactly, and independent Tesseract OCR reads `Narration selected area 71`. Annotation neither creates an extra History record nor changes the clipboard. Stopping the main recording preserves its frozen conversation owner. Exact ordered image bytes, prompts and model/effort reach both capture cleanup and the subsequent follow-up through the real Codex transport. Returning to the parent shows the saved pixels and reply.

The preparation-failure flow holds the external Codex model response, attaches a real selected image and opens the editor, then returns an empty model catalog. The actual preparation failure occurs before any PCM process starts. Both implementations retain the image under a recoverable History entry with the same message, clear pending ownership and make no speech or rewrite request. Application shutdown leaves external editors open as in the release; the observer stops them only after checking this behavior. Closed-state comparisons retain durable data, clipboard, requests and process ownership; they do not compare disposed GTK widgets.

| Retired Python contract | Native owner |
| --- | --- |
| Stop waits for selection; conversation ownership stays frozen | Existing screenshot owner, including continuation and invalid selection; new actual bridge/editor flow |
| Ordered image context and saved edits reach follow-ups | New joined flow checks exact annotated PNG and complete Codex inputs; existing owner checks frozen processing bytes |
| Incognito cancels selection without upload | Existing application screenshot owner |
| Remove/delete erase owned images | Existing owner, including editors saving on TERM and ignoring TERM |
| Preparation failure preserves attached screenshots | New real model-response failure before audio startup |
| Annotation cancellation and Undo/Redo | Existing [actual editor owner](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/narration-evidence.md) |

The 222-line `linux/tests/screenshot_workspace_smoke.py` and its recorder/speech/preparation replacements are retired. Shared Python rendering, screenshot and app-server helpers retain other consumers. The new canonical Make target passes with positively verified Python/uv traps unused; the old documented command fails at its interpreter trap. The existing seventeen-workflow/79-state screenshot owner and its SQLite-write and late-cancellation faults pass unchanged. A shared test-only normalizer replaces the duplicated narration-offset normalization; it changes no production code. Generated identities are mapped consistently and offsets must remain in `[0, 8)` before normalization. Exact bytes, captions and preview hashes remain compared.

The first native joined comparison passed all active states, exact annotation and both wide layouts, then exposed an observer error comparing effective visibility after shutdown. The final observers compare own visibility while active and durable results after shutdown. No production repair was needed. The reference accessibility client emits a `GetItems` cache warning while discovering the two applications; both private registry readiness checks pass, and actual editor actions and export complete. Native/editor logs contain no corresponding accessibility failure. Both implementations emit the same minimum-height allocation warning, requesting 561 pixels with 520 available. This is a bounded X11 comparison, not physical microphone, compositor-key or performance acceptance.

Final validation also passes the default fifteen-workflow/147-state application and command/settings owners, all 24 narration CLI cases plus three ownership faults, and the actual editor's pixels/OCR, Cancel and Undo/Redo. `make test` passes 139 tests with zero failures and 68 environment checks ignored across 98 suites; both strict Clippy configurations, formatting, generated consistency, full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Remaining Python passes 571 tests plus Ruff/formatting for 151 files. A repeat gate initially exceeded Unix-socket path length because its scratch wrapper omitted the established short `TMPDIR`; restoring it passes the same delivery check and the full gate without a source change. The failed and corrected receipts remain in `tmp/native-images-reviewed-native.log` and `tmp/native-images-reviewed-native-short.log`. The existing PyGObject warning remains.

Substantial review separates production +0/-0, Make/runner tooling +35/-0, tests/support +722/-246 and the independent 1,559-line/171,191-byte fixture; documentation is separate. No production test seam or second root harness is introduced, and every retired assertion has a remaining owner above.

The runner needs its usual Rust/bubblewrap/Xvfb/Openbox/session-accessibility prerequisites, ImageMagick, Xdotool, Tesseract and the verified editor artifact. Supply its absolute path with `MLUVA_TEST_EDITOR`; the default is `tmp/narrated-editor/tensaku`. A focused replay is `bash linux/tests/run_application_smoke.sh images wide /absolute/path/to/tensaku`; `screenshots` selects the existing lifecycle owner. Each run creates fresh evidence under `tmp/application/`, private HOME/XDG, buses, network/PID namespaces and masked system devices. Host focus, pointer, clipboard, microphone, credentials and user data remain untouched.

Raw source receipts are in `tmp/native-images-reviewed-source-*-evidence/`; final native Make/trap receipts are in `tmp/native-images-reviewed-traps-evidence/` and `tmp/native-images-reviewed-traps.log`. The initial four exact comparisons use `tmp/application/run.ZAuTgo/` and `tmp/native-images-pixels-*.txt`; the final Make run independently checks the frozen hashes. Complete Live/image and other joined workflows, actual Wayland/Omarchy selection and widget upgrade, physical keys/audio, clean distribution, remaining Python removal and current performance measurements remain required. All whole-workflow acceptance rows stay Pending; installed app/widget remain v1.6.0.
